# CardPulse

> An iPhone app for tracking what trading cards are worth. One watchlist, live
> market prices, a push notification when a card hits a price you set, and the
> return on each card since the day you added it.

CardPulse is published by Han Wong and is independent — not affiliated with
Nintendo, The Pokémon Company, PSA, eBay, or TCGplayer. It is a tracking tool,
not a marketplace: you cannot buy or sell cards in it.

- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/cardpulse-card-tracker/id6762569336
- Platform: iOS 15.1 or later. iPhone only. No Android or web version.
- Price: free with a 5-item watchlist and 3 active alerts. Premium is $4.99/month
  or $29.99/year.

## Definitions

These terms are CardPulse's own. Each has one canonical definition, on one page.

- **Returns since added** — the change in a card's market price measured from the
  moment it was added to a watchlist. The starting price is observed by the app
  at that moment, never estimated and never backdated to a purchase price the app
  does not know. https://getcardpulse.app/returns
- **Today's return** — the same card measured against yesterday's recorded close
  rather than against the starting price. Prints an em dash, not a zero, when no
  previous close exists. https://getcardpulse.app/returns
- **Demand pressure** — sales a day as a share of active listings for one card,
  on a scale from heavy supply to very tight, derived from eBay listing data.
- **Supply saturation** — active listings measured against the card's own 30-day
  baseline, so a rising number means supply is loosening.
- **Grading verdict** — the expected value of sending a raw card to PSA, computed
  across the PSA 10 / 9 / 8 / lower outcome distribution, net of grading cost.
- **Price alert** — a target on the raw, ungraded market price of one card. It
  fires once when the price crosses the target.
  https://getcardpulse.app/price-alerts

## Where the numbers come from

Raw card prices are TCGPlayer Market Price. Graded prices and sold aggregates
come from eBay sold listings. PSA population figures come from PSA's own census.
Price history is a daily series CardPulse records itself, so a day-over-day
change compares one source with itself rather than two feeds with each other.
Fair-value predictions are a model over pull cost, desirability and listing
dynamics — labelled as a model, not as a price.

## What CardPulse does not do

- It does not sell cards, take payment for cards, or list them.
- It does not know what you paid for a card and does not ask.
- It does not give financial advice, and a return figure is not a recommendation.
- It does not track you across other apps.
- Graded price alerts do not exist: there is no graded price feed to honour them.
